name: Sydney

supply.note: Greater Sydney draws chiefly on catchment storages managed by WaterNSW, with the Kurnell desalination plant and some groundwater. Shares withheld under Rule 9.5: no annual production mix with a year attached has been captured.

freshness_note: Prices are set for the financial year; the applicable rate is not. It switches with Greater Sydney storage, so this record carries a dated state observation that will need re-reading in a way no tariff document does.
open_items: The retail trigger mechanics, which decide the rate only near a crossing and cannot change it at 92% storage.
A storage history series, needed if a past benchmark date is ever priced.
grade_note: Grade B. Every rate is published and sourced; what is not established is which of two published rates applies today. At A$3.41/kL the standardized supply bill is A$59.97 a month; at the drought rate of A$3.84/kL it is A$66.42 — a spread of 10.8%, far above the 1% ceiling that separates Grade B from Grade A.
methodology_note: Sydney is the first city in the Index whose published price depends on a physical measurement that changes weekly. Every cadence class in §6 assumes a document that is revised on a schedule; a storage-triggered tariff is not that. A tariff whose applicable rate is state-dependent needs its own freshness class, and the state itself needs to be stored as a dated observation rather than read at publication time.
services_note: Unlike Perth, Sydney's total water services figure is comparable. The wastewater service charge is a fixed amount that Sydney Water states already contains a deemed amount for usage, so it rests on the connection rather than on a property valuation.
resolution_note: The first city in the Index whose applicable rate required two pieces of evidence: the tariff rule from Sydney Water and a dated state observation from WaterNSW. Storage at 92%, drought rate engaging below 60%, so the normal rate applies and the tariff state is recorded rather than assumed.
